identity.operation: Unpack an object member with a nested array format through unpack_array.
identity.condition: The member, such as data in {"data":42}, has the wrong type.
identity.capability: Pass the member key as parent_key to the array type guard and expose its diagnostic.
identity.consequence: The member uses o; the only [o!] call is for a root array, so the keyed array diagnostic is not reached.

requirement: Object-field unpacking must reach the supported wrong-type diagnostic for an expected nested array with its field key.

assessment.requirement: Within object-member unpacking, a format expecting an array must be reachable with a wrong-type member so the supported array diagnostic can include that member's key.
assessment.target_route: A finite input consisting of a selector byte followed by {"data":42} parses as an object. A member-array format would make unpack_object look up data, pass its key to unpack, and dispatch '[' to unpack_array's wrong-type guard.
assessment.failure_condition: The old entry instead calls "{s?o}" for object members; o accepts the integer. Its only array format, "[o!]", is called only when the root is already an array, and top-level unpack starts with a null parent key. The entry also calls json_unpack without an error object, so it cannot expose diagnostic text.
assessment.alternative_paths: The root "o" call only returns the object. Changing JSON bytes cannot change either fixed format or the root-array guard; deep copy and dump do not invoke unpack_array.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The object member lookup forwards its key to the child unpack operation.
The child '[' format dispatches to unpack_array with that key.
The old member's o format accepts the value without array type validation.
Top-level unpack supplies a null key.
json_unpack supplies no error object and uses default flags.
The added API check establishes the supported keyed array wrong-type diagnostic.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: The entry maps a finite selector-plus-JSON byte sequence to a parsed root.

necessity_evidence.reason: Object-member array validation is part of the unpack format protocol. The changed source supports a keyed wrong-type diagnostic, but the old target fixes the member format to `o` and supplies no error object. Its root-array call cannot reach the same keyed diagnostic.
necessity_evidence.finite_witness: A selector byte 0x00 followed by {"data":42} reaches the object's `data` member. With the supported setup `json_unpack_ex(root, &error, 0, "{s[i]}", "data")`, the source reports “Expected array, got integer for key data”. The old entry instead calls `json_unpack(root, "{s?o}", "data", &field)`.

coverage_witness.supported_behavior: An object-member array format reports a wrong-type error that names the member key.
coverage_witness.required_setup: Parse {"data":42}, then unpack with an array format for `data` and an error object, as in `json_unpack_ex(root, &error, 0, "{s[i]}", "data")`.
coverage_witness.actual_target_setup: For objects, the entry calls `json_unpack` with `o` and `{s?o}`; it calls `[o!]` only for an array root.
coverage_witness.blocked_behavior: The keyed “Expected array, got integer for key data” diagnostic cannot be reached.
coverage_witness.equivalent_routes: None in the complete old entry: `o` accepts the member, while `[o!]` runs only on an array root with no parent key.
